subject.title: fix(process): add zombie reaper to prevent child process leak

question: Should this PR be reworked into a true process-wait fix, accepted only as a bounded mitigation, or paused behind the linked production issue?
rationale: The remaining blocker is process-lifecycle direction plus availability proof; automation cannot safely decide whether a SIGCHLD nudge is acceptable for a production process-exhaustion bug.

options.title: Rework around the wait owner
options.body: Change the implementation so the owning OpenClaw path actually waits for the reported children, or add a real Linux wait/subreaper mechanism, then prove the direct-child zombie count drops on this head.

options.title: Accept only as mitigation
options.body: Maintainers could keep a best-effort nudge if the PR stops claiming to close the production leak and adds mitigation-scoped proof.

options.title: Pause behind the issue
options.body: Keep the linked issue canonical until a reproducible process-tree trace identifies the right owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Rework around the wait owner
recommendation.body: Change the implementation so the owning OpenClaw path actually waits for the reported children, or add a real Linux wait/subreaper mechanism, then prove the direct-child zombie count drops on this head.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subprocess and service-managed child lifecycle work makes this the best available routing candidate for the wait-boundary decision.
